section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1976
title: Causes of Suicides The total number of suicides reported during 1976 has been classified under different heads and the last category 'Other causes' covers the unspecified causes of suicides. The major cause of suicides during 1976 was 'Despair over dreadful diseases' (19.5 percent). The second important cause was 'Quarrel with parents-in-law' (9.1 percent), followed by 'Quarrel with Spouses' (6.3 percent). 'Love Affairs' (5.4 percent) 'Dispute over Property' (3.8 percent), 'Poverty' (3.7 percent), 'Insanity' (2.7 percent) and 'Failure in examination' (2.1 percent). The causes comparatively less important were 'Unemployment' (1.4 percent), 'Bankruptcy' (1.0 percent), 'Fall in Social reputation' (0.7 percent) and 'Deaths of dear persons' (0.5 percent). The category 'Other causes' accounted for 43.8 percent of the total suicides registered during 1976. The detailed statistics are presented in Table No. 2.
